newsitem.title: UK: U.S., British bonds look a firmer bet than stocks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., British bonds look a firmer bet than stocks.

text.p: U.S. and British bond markets look better value than stocks in the current climate of expected interest rate rises, but equity markets in Europe and Japan have investor appeal, analysts said on Friday.
"Markets will be looking to how things pan out in 1998, to see if the tightening process is going to be lengthy," said Stephen Hannah, chief economist at IBJ International here.
U.S. and other bond markets are already pricing in a quarter point rise in U.S. interest rates after the next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on March 25, analysts said.
The federal funds target rate currently stands at five percent.
